The '''16th Legislative Assembly of Karnataka''' was formed following the [[2023 Karnataka Legislative Assembly election|2023 Assembly election]] for all 224 seats.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-13 |title=Karnataka election results 2023: Full list of winners |url=https://indianexpress.com/elections/karnataka-election-results-full-list-of-winners-8606612/ |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref><ref>
{{Cite web |title=Karnataka Election Result 2023 Live: Karnataka Assembly Election Results - Congress celebrates party's impending victory |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/karnataka-assembly-election-results-2023-live-news-karnataka-cm-siddaramaiah-dk-shivakumar/liveblog/100195381.cms |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Karnataka Election Results 2023 Live Updates: Congress wins 136 seats, BJP 65, JDS 19 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/karnataka-election-result-2023-live-updates-vote-counting-bjp-congress-jds-2378541-2023-05-13 |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref> The election were held on 10 May 2023 and the results were declared on 13 May 2023.

==Leadership==
The assembly was initially governed by the [[Second Siddaramaiah ministry]], sworn in on 20 May 2023 with [[Siddaramaiah]] as Chief Minister and [[D. K. Shivakumar]] as Deputy Chief Minister. Following an internal Congress leadership transition, Siddaramaiah resigned on 29 May 2026. The [[D. K. Shivakumar ministry]] was sworn in on 3 June 2026, with D. K. Shivakumar as Chief Minister and [[G. Parameshwara]] as Deputy Chief Minister.
